name: McDonnell Douglas MD-80 / MD-90
summary: The stretched DC-9 descendants that formed the backbone of US airlines in the 1980s-2000s; the few remaining are largely retired or in charter and cargo roles.

wings: Low swept wing, relatively small for the fuselage
engines: Two engines on the rear fuselage sides, long slim JT8D nacelles on MD-80s and bigger, fatter V2500 nacelles on the MD-90
tail: T-tail with a tall swept fin

tellTales: Very long, thin fuselage with two rear-mounted engines and a T-tail
Small wing relative to the long body, with no winglets

confusedWith.howToTell: The 717 is noticeably shorter, with fatter, shorter-cowled BR715 engines; the MD-80 is a longer stretch with slimmer JT8D nacelles.
The 737 has its engines slung under the wings and a conventional tail; the MD-80 has rear-mounted engines and a T-tail.

usCount.source: FAA Releasable Aircraft Database — valid registrations
